## T2379 — a directly checked later address,2026-11-04

Fergus, *Directory of the City of Chicago,1839* (Chicago:Fergus Printing Company,1876), Hotels section printed p.37, gives “Lake House, cor. Rush and North Water sts”. The actual line was directly read in the Allen County Public Library Genealogy Center scan on Internet Archive, official image https://archive.org/download/fergusdirectoryo00ferg/page/n48.jpg . This verifies ONE entry's printing, not the historical accuracy of Fergus's later recollection or the whole directory's OCR. Existing source `fergus_chicago_directory_1839` is reused; tier2, text_only, publication1876 and described1839 remain. No duplicate source, phase or grade is introduced.

The later Rush/North Water address differs from Andreas's Rush/Kinzie/Michigan account and is retained as counterevidence for a future period-map/conveyance adjudication. The 1843-canvass/1896-edition west-half-block description remains a transcription-mediated lead, not a metric plan. Neither later account locates the July1835 construction shell. Do not silently equate North Water with Michigan or move the record to a modern Wrigley gloss.

The bounded fulltext search covered28 actual primary transcriptions (15Democrat,13American;3,215,983characters), all corpus-SHA verified. Only the already-admittedJune10 project notice appeared under the named/OCR patterns;12 broader candidate contexts were checked and concerned other buildings or places. Newspaper readings remain transcription-mediated: no originalJune10facsimile was read, damagedOCR may miss notices, and this is not proof of absence. The existing one-story4m roofless24x15m shell, its placement/phase/confidence, the later1856picture's date limit, and the original incomplete image acceptance remain unchanged.
